answer: Memory-hard identity minting resists sybils: minting each key requires a function that fills and repeatedly reads a large memory block, so cost is bound by RAM capacity and bandwidth, not core count. A farm runs many threads, but each needs its own big buffer; sharing fails because the work is one long dependent thread of reads. Cheap parallelism turns hollow — a thousand clones need a thousand full memory arenas at once. Core-only proof-of-work is a relic here; memory bandwidth is the bottleneck capping how fast one operator can forge identities.
